335932.title: Balog–Roche-Newton–Zhelezov growth conjecture for difference sets
335932.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of scalars with at least three elements, and put $D=A-A$. For a positive integer $m$, write $D^m$ for the $m$-fold product set of $D$. **Balog–Roche-Newton–Zhelezov growth conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, there is a universally and polynomially related positive integer $m$ such that

$$
|D^m|\geq |D|^n.
$$

This question was raised by Balog, Roche-Newton and Zhelezov in connection with multiplicative growth of difference sets. The source presents it as an open question and does not state a resolution.

336197.title: Distance-two antimagic labelling conjecture
336197.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges and no isolated edge. For each vertex $v$, let $S_v$ be the sum of the labels on edges incident with $v$. A **distance-two antimagic labelling** uses every label from $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ exactly once and requires the vertex sums to distinguish vertices at graph distance at most two. **Distance-two antimagic labelling conjecture.** There is a labelling of $G$ using every label from $[m]$ exactly once such that

$$
S_v\ne S_w
$$

for every pair of vertices $v,w$ with $d(v,w)\le 2$. This is proposed as a natural next step toward the full antimagic labelling conjecture; its status is left open in the paper.

336513.title: Higher-order Jensen-polynomial real-rootedness conjecture for the partition function
336513.statement:
Let $p(n)$ denote the number of partitions of the positive integer $n$. For a positive integer $m$, define the Jensen polynomial

$$
J_{m,n}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^m {m\choose k}p(n+k)x^k.
$$

**Partition-function Jensen-polynomial conjecture.** For every positive integer $m\geq 4$, there exists a positive integer $N(m)$ such that, for every $n\geq N(m)$, the polynomial $J_{m,n}(x)$ has only real zeros.

This proposes eventual real-rootedness for all higher-degree Jensen polynomials of the partition function. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture.

338138.title: The conjecture that all trees are neighborhood-prime
338138.statement:
A **neighborhood-prime labeling** of a graph with $n$ vertices is a bijection from its vertices to $\\{1,2,\ldots,n\\}$ such that the labels of the open neighborhood of every vertex of degree at least $2$ have greatest common divisor $1$. A graph admitting such a labeling is called **neighborhood-prime**.

**Neighborhood-prime tree conjecture.** Every tree is neighborhood-prime.

Neighborhood-prime labelings are known for many classes of trees, including paths, caterpillars, banana trees, lobsters, spiders, full binary trees, and complete binary trees. The conjecture asks whether this property holds for all trees.

338758.title: The Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for even cycles and paths
338758.statement:
Let $n\ge3$ and $k\ge2$. For each $i\in\{0,1,\ldots,n-2\}$, let $G_i=P_{2i+3}$, and let $G_{n-1}$ be either $C_{2n}$ or $P_{2n+1}$. Choose integers $i_1,\ldots,i_k$ satisfying

$$
n-1\ge i_1\ge\cdots\ge i_k\ge0.
$$

Here $GR(G_{i_1},\ldots,G_{i_k})$ is the least order of a complete graph such that every Gallai edge-coloring using at most $k$ colors contains a monochromatic copy of $G_{i_j}$ in color $j$ for some $j$. **The Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for even cycles and paths.** For all such $n$, $k$, and indices,

$$
GR(G_{i_1},\ldots,G_{i_k})=|G_{i_1}|+\sum_{j=2}^k i_j.
$$

The displayed quantity is known to be a lower bound by an explicit Gallai-coloring construction; the conjecture asserts that this lower bound is always sharp. The source gives no resolution of the general upper bound.

340259.title: The Siemons–Wagner conjecture on primitive permutation groups and subset orbit sizes
340259.statement:
Let $G$ be a primitive permutation group acting on a set $\Omega$ of cardinality $n\ge 8$. For a subset $S\subseteq \Omega$, write $S^G$ for its orbit under $G$. **Siemons–Wagner conjecture.** If there exists a $3$-subset $\Delta\subseteq \Omega$ such that

$$
|\Delta^G|>|\Sigma^G|
$$

for every $4$-subset $\Sigma$ containing $\Delta$, then $G\cong PSL(2,7)$ or $G\cong PGL(2,7)$. This conjecture identifies the two exceptional primitive groups whose orbit structure on $3$- and $4$-subsets has the stated inequality; the surrounding argument establishes the claim for the remaining families considered there, while the full assertion is left as a conjecture.

341596.title: Berge cycle conjecture for uniform covering hypergraphs
341596.statement: Let a **$k$-uniform covering hypergraph** be a hypergraph in which every hyperedge has size $k$ and every pair of vertices is contained in a hyperedge. Let $n$ be the number of vertices and $m$ the number of hyperedges. A **Berge cycle of length $s$** consists of distinct vertices $v_1,\ldots,v_s$ and distinct hyperedges $e_1,\ldots,e_s$ such that $\{v_i,v_{i+1}\}\subseteq e_i$ for each $i$, with indices taken modulo $s$. **The covering-hypergraph Berge cycle conjecture.** For all $k\geq 4$, every $k$-uniform covering hypergraph on $n$ vertices with at least $m\geq 3$ hyperedges contains a Berge cycle of length $s$ for $3\leq s\leq\min(m,n)$. This extends the paper's results for covering hypergraphs with hyperedges of size at most $3$; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

341663.title: Grünbaum–Kalai–Sarkaria face-number conjecture
341663.statement:
For a simplicial complex $S$, let $f_i(S)$ denote the number of its $i$-dimensional faces. A **$d$-complex** is a simplicial complex of dimension $d$, and $S$ is **embeddable in $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$** when it admits a topological embedding there.

**Grünbaum–Kalai–Sarkaria conjecture.** For every $d\geq 1$, there is a constant $C_d$ such that

$$
f_d(S)\leq C_d f_{d-1}(S)
$$

for every $d$-complex $S$ embeddable in $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$.

This conjecture generalizes the planar inequality relating edges and vertices. The source says that the question is open and that work of Kalai and Sarkaria suggests a sharper formulation determining the best possible constant in each dimension.

341664.title: A face-number bound for embeddable simplicial complexes
341664.statement:
For a simplicial complex $S$, let $f_i(S)$ denote the number of its $i$-dimensional faces; in this formulation, $f_d$ is the number of $d$-faces and $f_0$ the number of vertices.

**Face-number bound.** For every $d\geq 1$, there is a constant $C_d$ such that

$$
f_d\leq C_d f_0^d.
$$

The source presents this as another possible generalization of the planar edge–vertex inequality. It does not specify the class of complexes or embeddings in the displayed statement, and gives no resolution, so the claim is recorded as open with low confidence.

343072.title: Conjecture on uniform spectral separation implying injectivity
343072.statement: Let $F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^n$ be a $C^1$ map. Suppose there exists an $\varepsilon>0$ such that $|\lambda|\geqslant\varepsilon$ for every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $F'(x)$ and every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$. **Uniform spectral injectivity conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $F$ is injective. The result is stated as a higher-dimensional extension of the two-dimensional injectivity theorem discussed in the paper; the surrounding text says that the claim is true when $n=2$, while its status in general dimension is not specified here.

343469.title: The generalized 2-adic valuation conjecture for weighted Catalan numbers
343469.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $L_n^{(k)}$ denote the weighted Catalan numbers with weight $b(x)=(2x+1)^{2k}$. Let $C_n$ be the Catalan numbers, let $s_2(n)$ denote the sum of the binary digits of $n$, and let $\xi_2$ denote the 2-adic valuation.

**Generalized 2-adic valuation conjecture.** There exists a 2-adic integer $\alpha_k$ and a nonnegative integer $c_k$ such that

$$
\xi_2(L_n^{(k)}-C_n)=s_2(n)+\xi_2(n-\alpha_k)+c_k
$$

for all $n\geq 2$.

The authors present this as a generalization of Postnikov's conjecture and note that analogous behavior was not observed for other polynomial weight functions; the excerpt gives no proof or resolution.

344479.title: Eventual hyperbolicity conjecture for Jensen polynomials of k-regular partitions
344479.statement:
For an integer $k\geq2$, let $p_k(n)$ count the partitions of $n$ having no parts divisible by $k$, so that

$$
\sum_{n\geq0}p_k(n)q^n=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1-q^{kn}}{1-q^n}.
$$

For integers $d\geq1$ and $n\geq0$, let $J_{p_k}^{d,n}(X)$ be the degree-$d$ Jensen polynomial associated with the sequence $p_k(n)$.

**k-regular Jensen polynomial conjecture.** Let $d\geq1$ and $k\geq2$ be integers. There exists a positive integer $N(d)$ such that $J_{p_k}^{d,n}(X)$ is hyperbolic for all $n\geq N(d)$.

Here hyperbolic means that all roots are real. The paper states this as an equivalent reformulation of the higher-order Turán claim and then proves the stronger result for $k$-regular partition functions.

344496.title: Compact graph-induced semiseparable representations for two-dimensional mesh graphs
344496.statement:
Let $M\times M$ 2D mesh graphs be graphs with the corresponding vertex sets $\mathbb{V}_\mathbb{G}$, and let a **Hamiltonian path** be a path $\mathbb{P}$ visiting every vertex exactly once. A **GIRS-$c$ pair** is a pair $(A,\mathbb{G})$ satisfying the paper's GIRS rank bound. **Mesh-graph compact representation conjecture.** There exists a constant $\gamma\geq 1$ such that for all $M\times M$ 2D mesh graphs $\mathbb{G}$ there exists a Hamiltonian path $\mathbb{P}$ such that, if $(A,\mathbb{G})$ is GIRS-$c$, then $(A,\mathbb{G})$ possesses a $\mathbb{G}$-SS representation with

$$
r_i^g,r_i^h\leq c\gamma
$$

for every $i\in\mathbb{V}_\mathbb{G}$. This is the paper's more specific conjecture for a family of graphs; the source gives no resolution.

344631.title: Brill–Noether non-existence conjecture for real divisors
344631.statement:
Let $g\geq 1$. **Brill–Noether non-existence conjecture for real divisors.** There exists a family of undirected, connected multigraphs, one for each genus, such that for every pair of real numbers $r\geq 0$ and $0\leq d\leq 2g-2$, if

$$
\rho(g,r,d)=g-(r+1)(g-d+r)<0,
$$

then the graph in the family has no $\mathbb{R}$-divisor of degree at most $d$ and rank equal to $r$. Together with the existence conjecture, this would provide a graph-theoretic Brill–Noether existence and non-existence theory parallel to that for general algebraic curves.

344632.title: Covering radius conjecture for graph critical sets
344632.statement:
Let $G$ be an undirected, connected multigraph with genus $g\geq 1$ and $n\geq 2$ vertices. Let $\mathcal{N}_G$, ${\rm Crit}_{\triangle}(L_G)$ and ${\rm Crit}_{\bar{\triangle}}(L_G)$ be the three sets associated with the graph Laplacian, and let $P_{1,\lambda}$ be the stated polytope. **Covering radius conjecture for graph critical sets.** For every $\lambda\in[1/g,g]$, the covering radii of all three sets with respect to the distance function induced by $P_{1,\lambda}$ are at least

$$
\frac{\sqrt{g/\lambda}}{n}.
$$

The proposition preceding the conjecture identifies the relevant covering radii, while the conjecture extends the non-special-divisor formulation to the two critical sets.

348799.title: Balister et al.'s partition conjecture for vectors over \(\mathbb{F}_2^n\)
348799.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_{2^{n-1}}\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be nonzero, not necessarily distinct, vectors satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{2^{n-1}}v_i=0.
$$

**Balister et al.'s partition conjecture.** There exists a partition of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ into pairs of vectors $\{p_i,q_i\}$, for $i=1,\ldots,2^{n-1}$, such that

$$
v_i=p_i-q_i
$$

for every $i$. Cases up to $n\leq 5$ have been proved, but the general statement remains open and is used in the paper as a tool toward the Odd Tree Conjecture.

349179.title: Prime-order balanced shift-pattern coloring conjecture
349179.statement: Let $G_{m,n}$ be the grid in question, and let a shifted $k$-subgrid mean a $k$-subgrid satisfying the paper's shift-pattern condition. **Prime-order balanced coloring conjecture.** For prime $k$, there exists a $k$-coloring of $G_{k^2,k^2}$ with shift pattern on $k$-subgrids such that each color occurs exactly $k$ times in each subgrid. This implies that there is a $k$-coloring of $G_{k^2+k,k}$ with shifted $k$-subgrid on the $k^2$ by $k^2$ part and monochromatic stripes on the last $k$ rows. The claim is motivated by constructions observed for $k\in\{2,3,5\}$ and would extend the known $k$-colorability of $G_{k^2+k,k}$ to a structured construction for every prime $k$.

359361.title: Hanson–Toft conjecture on the minimum size of clique co-critical graphs
359361.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$, let $t_1,\ldots,t_k$ be positive integers, and let

$$
r=r(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_k}).
$$

A non-complete graph $G$ is **$(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_k})$-co-critical** if $G\not\rightarrow(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_k})$, but $G+e\rightarrow(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_k})$ for every edge $e$ in $\overline G$. **Hanson and Toft's conjecture.** Every $(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_k})$-co-critical graph on $n$ vertices has at least

$$
(r-2)(n-r+2)+\binom{r-2}{2}
$$

edges, and this bound is best possible for every $n$. The construction $K_{r-2}+\overline K_{n-r+2}$ attains the bound when $n\geq r$, but the supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved in full generality.

362860.title: Pattern-avoidance image conjecture for looms
362860.statement:
Given a set of permutations $S$, let $\operatorname{Av}(S)$ denote the set of permutations avoiding the patterns in $S$. Let $\mathfrak{L}_{n,m}$ be the family of looms and let $\gamma_{n,m}$ be the map from looms to permutations. **Pattern-avoidance image conjecture.** For every $n,m\geq 1$, there exists a set of permutations $S_{n,m}$ such that

$$
\gamma_{n,m}(\mathfrak{L}_{n,m})=\operatorname{Av}(S_{n,m}).
$$

This predicts that the image of the loom family is a permutation class described by pattern avoidance; the supplied text gives no evidence of resolution.

376066.title: Baker's Brill-Noether existence conjecture for finite graphs
376066.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, undirected, connected, loop-free multigraph of genus $g$. Define the Brill-Noether number by

$$
\rho(g,r,d)=g-(r+1)(g-d+r).
$$

A divisor on $G$ has a degree and a rank in the usual graph-theoretic sense. **Brill-Noether existence conjecture for graphs.** For every pair of non-negative integers $r_0,d_0$ satisfying $\rho(g,r_0,d_0)\geq 0$, there is a divisor $D$ on $G$ of degree $d_0$ and rank at least $r_0$; equivalently, there is a divisor of degree at most $d_0$ and rank equal to $r_0$.

This is the graph-theoretic analogue of the existence part of the classical Brill-Noether theorem. The paper identifies this conjecture as its principal focus; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied material.
